Name: Urgent
Description:
# Context

## Customer message

In Slack, everything is urgent. In Peek, we give users option to say what's urgent and needs immediate response and properly highlighting it to the receiver user.

## Problem

Peek is all about being focused and not turning real-time communication in endless stream of notifications. That's why mentions don't trigger notification and red banners as in Slack. It's just way to say "this person should eventually read it". Though, sometimes things are urgent.

If you need urgent immediate response from others, we want to give you a way how to do it. The goal is to give you a clear way how to escalate time-sensitive message that will notify the right person, without such message being lost in other non-urgent communications.

# Solution

## Writing urgent message

When contacting somebody or some group, you use `@`. If you need the message to be treated as urgent you simply add `!` before it. E.g.:

| Type | Mention | Urgent mention |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Person | @Katerina | !@Katerina |
| Team | @design-team | !@design-team |

Sometimes in messages, you mention multiple people. But only for one it should be urgent where for others it's should be treated as normal message.

> !@Mike We found critical issue. Can you take a look why those emails are not being sent?
>
> cc @cs-team we have potential issue with emails not working

For Mike it's urgent message. But for customer support team it's just regular new conversation that will appear in Screener.

## Receiving urgent message

At Desk, if you have at least one urgent message, we show dedicated section in the top with those urgent messages. They are not going through Screener, but immediately "interrupt" your work.

## Future exploration

### Mobile app push notifications

Once we have mobile app, generally there won't be much notification. The urgent conversation should be exception.

# Usage scenarios

## Writing message that is urgent

We might explore different ways how to say it's urgent in future, but the primary way to make it urgent for somebody is simply by using ! before the mention. E.g. `!@Katerina`.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/f8886170-d80c-4598-be67-0cf3f4dfd2a2/a4ed8395-b446-4ba2-95c7-e9c7841d849c)

## Receiving urgent message

You have a two main ways how to spot urgent message. 

1. At Desk new section Urgent will appear with that conversation.

   ![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/2f8d7dd6-77fe-4d20-97a2-90c7b38db394/f57fb1ec-b588-4bf8-a1bb-bc04e7c01155)
2. As you browsing through Topics, People,.. urgent conversation will have special indication like red dot (instead of blue dot)

   ![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/8158f0e0-8e22-401f-89e3-25594ddf02e3/09a8e8ae-78da-446a-8b59-594491dcfdb7)

## Message sent, but post-hoc making it urgent

Sometimes you send message and at the moment it's not urgent. The receiver doesn't response. Time is flying and suddenly the issue is more pressing. You should have a way to make the message urgent by e.g. editing the original message and adding `!` before the mention and saving the message.

If user read the message, just didn't response. The conversation still should be put into the Urgent to make sure that the message is not forgotten and it's answered.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/7ed1ccab-8f14-4560-84a6-08667d3fe756/05706563-9cfa-40e7-a8c8-1212b8557ca5)

## You mention more people/groups, but only for some it's urgent

One message can be urgent for some, but not for others. That's why the `!` needs to be used with every mention. E.g.

> !@Adam !@Bob @Cathy some message

It will make the message Urgent for Adam and Bob, but not for Cathy. It seems bit cumbersome to  always add the `!`, but that's kind a the point. It should be used only if something is truly urgent and it should be very specific for whom it's urgent.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/61b1646d-6c01-4271-a0e2-b50371791bf7/399e818a-dc95-4fff-8a70-ff962e5801a6)

## You checked the urgent message, you reply and now you're receiving following replies

Using `!@mention` is one time thing. If you checked the conversation, and make it "read", then you have option to add it to Open Work so you can stay up to date. But new replies will not put the conversation again to Urgent, unless somebody again specifically mention you using `!@mention`.

Name: Screener
Description:
# Context

## Customer message

You should be in charge of your focus. Not others. Screener gives you option to quickly scan incoming messages and decide when you will deal with it.

## Problem

When you open Slack you see all the new activity and channels indicating mention and new conversation. To review them, you actually have to read them. It push users to always be in reactive mode trying to read every message as it appears in user's Slack.

With Peek we want to be different, the goal is allow users to do screening of incoming message and decide when and how user will tackle it.

# Solution

In the desk at the top, if user gets mention in new conversation (or topics), such conversation will appear in Screener. User only now that there are incoming messages.

Once it expands it, they get list of incoming conversations with sneak peak of what's the conversation about.

Users can perform 3 actions:

* **Add to open work items** — to the main list where users organize the current work.
* **Later** — with option to specify when it should appear again (15 mins, 1 hour, 3 hours, tomorrow,..). Once user clicks Later, the conversation disappears from Screener. It will again appear there based on the set up timing.
* **Dismiss** —  conversation will be removed. User can still find the message through regular browsing of Peek, but it won't appear in Screener anymore.

## Future exploration

### Focus mode

If Peek has some kind of focus mode — user indicates that they are in deep work and don't want to be distracted — we might not even show new incoming messages to completely remove fear-of-missing out. 

### Hover preview

If user hover over the conversation, we might show the whole conversation in temporary modal to give user better understanding what's about.

# Usage scenarios

## No new incoming messages

When user doesn't have any new incoming messages, we won't show the Screener section at all.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/96333137-265b-443d-a26f-d9ef299941de/1375cd4f-4335-4403-941a-090edc4b0103)

## Incoming conversation -> open work item

If user evaluate the message is important and they want to focus on it right away, they simply add it to open work. The conversation will appear as new item in[ Open work](<https://linear.app/peek-app/project/open-working-items-2d7ecfd63552/overview>) section.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/c39bb2a7-a9b9-4007-a656-b9be20fe7ba3/0d4e81d3-eab9-440c-a762-b8d546e10698)

## Incoming conversation -> later

If user thinks the message is interesting, but don't have space to deal with it right now, user will click button Later and decide when the conversation should re-appear in Screener. In the meantime the conversation will disappear from Screener.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/44550341-300d-4c5d-8bad-9b7a10ea1329/d2505cd4-7963-4aee-886e-461ccfdf3d2e)

## Incoming conversation -> dismiss

If user thinks that the message is not really relevant or for sure not to deal with it anytime soon, user simply dismiss it. The conversation will be still treated as Unread during regular browsing of Peek, but it won't be shown anywhere in Desk.

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/5f0076a2-29df-4a05-8275-b32720956024/5604673d-14cd-4463-86e3-16c3b7ae7caa)

Name: Open working items
Summary: Manage work you want to focus on.
Description:
# Context

## Customer message

Desk is about organizing your work. Open working items is the key way to do it. It's like tabs in browser. You decide what to have open, what to be focusing on, and what not. You can open anything in open work —  conversations, topics, views, …

## Problem

One struggle Slack users have is how to keep focusing on the work **you** want to focus on. The endless highlights of unread channels and new mentions and reactions always push you towards reading something else than you want to focus on. Then when you finally want to focus on the longer message you want to post in thread, you suddenly don't remember where the thread was.

Whole point of Desk is to have place that it's yours. You organize what you want to read, write, work on. Open work items is in center because it allows you to organize things you want to focus on now, soon, or simply keep it open for the very first moment once you have time for it.

# Solution

Open work is like tabs in browser. You click on tab you want to read or write to. You close the one that you're no longer interested in. You open as new item almost anything across Peek to add it to the list for near later.

Typically you will add to open work things like:

* conversations
* topics
* views
* files
* DMs or Teams

## Future exploration

### Set aside / groups / workspaces

This feature was inspired by the most popular feature in browsers — tabs. In last years, browsers add different ways how to organize tabs. Like grouping them, putting them aside, or organizing them via workspaces. We might in future explore different ways how to give people even more capabilities to organize what they want to focus on and when.

Maybe you could easily save tabs, selected tabs or the whole group to Starred under a folder.

# Usage scenarios

## Open item from Screener

Someone else start brand new conversation and mention you. You check it out through Screener and decide to add to Open work.

## Open item as your browsing through Peek

As user you can be browsing through Peek and spot something, that you want to study more deeply later on, simply watch the discussion going forward or even actively participate in such discussion. In all cases, you can always middle-click on the link for the conversation or use context menu and add it to Open work.

Once we have mobile app, we can have a concept of long tap on the conversation / link automatically adding it to Open work.

Important note. It's not just conversation. You can open Views, DMs, Files,…

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/496d8113-46e8-4a5a-b037-3beae58aa2ae/1a557172-2fe8-4b29-b4e7-21a37cc5da98)

## Close item as you're done with it

When you're done reading, you can simply close the "tab".

![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/4028fe1e-53e0-4f34-9f7f-d8f4d8889532/4aa2a50d-12e2-4697-8b11-d0a1f33f776c/027aa636-9324-466c-8747-543218dcd6cb)

## New activity happen to e.g. conversation that you have open

When you have open "tab" with some conversation. You're not focused on the tab and the conversation has new replies / activity. We should indicate there is something new.

## Being in Open Work item and browsing

When you click on Open Work item and there is e.g. converation that mention other conversation. If you follow the 2nd conversation that becomes the current "state" of the tab. When you change to different tab and then back, you will get where you left off.

Name: Starred
Description:
# Context

## Customer message

Your Desk wouldn't be anything, if you don't have quick access to things you access frequently.  Starred is simply list with anything that you bookmarked in Peek.

## Problem

Open work is about things that you want to focus now or in near future. It's about organizing you work day. There are more long term things or regular habits that you want to have quick access from your Desk.

# Solution

Starred is simple list of anything (conversation, topic, tag/view, file, DM, team,..) that you bookmarked . You can reorder it in a way you want. You can see new activity indication to know there is something new.

### How is it different than Open work

Both Open work and Starred are list where you managed what you want to see and work with. It both belongs to your Desk, because it's about organizing your work.

So, how is it different?

Philosophically, open work is about what you want to focus "now" or near future (today). Open work tabs change through the day as you finish things and start new things.

Starred is about long-term things. It's about regular habits and quick access to them.

How is it different practically?

Open work acts as tab in browser. You can keep browsing and "changing the URL" and when you switch tab and later go back, you will continue exactly where you left off. Starred items doesn't change. When you click, it's always brings you to the very same place.

## Future exploration

### Folders

If user has too many starred items, the single list can become inconvenient. Organizing in folders that groups related things might be interesting option that users are used to from browsers.

# Usage scenarios

## Adding things in Starred

When you're on conversation detail, topic detail, view or file, there is always option to "star" it.

## Showing new activity for Starred item

When new activity happens in starred item, it will get highlighted.

## Browsing Starred item

When you click on starred item and keep exploring it, navigating to other conversations. Once you click again on Starred item, it will bring you back to the "saved" place.
